source.title: Multilingual Refusal Alignment for Safer Large Language Models
source.authors: Aleksandra Krasnodebska; Wojciech Kusa; Aldo Lipani

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates harmful-request ASR for released abliterated checkpoints, which bears on the practical effect in V2. It does not perform the ablation itself or measure a refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The authors state that they adopted abliterated Llama checkpoints and did not perform the ablation procedure. The paper reports roughly 20% ASR for the abliterated versions on RefusEU-test. DPO results are not treated as evidence about a removable direction because the training intentionally induces refusal behavior. The flattened Table 1 does not reliably support assigning its individual values to the abliterated checkpoint and language combinations.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates two released abliterated Llama-3.1 checkpoints (8B and 70B) against their instruct versions on harmful-request ASR in 12 European languages. That bears on V2 (practical removal) in a new multilingual setting. The authors did not compute or ablate a direction themselves. The DPO experiments deliberately induce refusal, so they are not evidence on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that English-only safety alignment does not reliably transfer to other languages, and that multilingual DPO (balanced or high-resource data) restores safety in abliterated models with small Global MMLU losses. Llama-70B preserves safety and language consistency better than 8B. Smaller models may need balanced data plus translation-based processing.
record.recipe_differences: The study adopts already-abliterated checkpoints and performs multilingual DPO training; it does not identify a difference-in-means direction or perform the original direction-ablation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety outcomes vary with training-data language configuration, evaluation language, and model size; the reported aggregate abliterated-checkpoint result does not resolve these differences separately.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (venue stated in metadata); the text identifies the paper as an arXiv preprint.
record.problems: The ablation was not performed by the authors. The approximate ASR statement is aggregate, and the flattened table does not reliably permit assigning its individual values to particular abliterated checkpoints and languages. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-linked rows extracted. Results for DPO-trained models reflect behavior deliberately induced by refusal-alignment training; the paper does not measure a refusal direction or its transfer. General-capability evaluations concern training variants, not the effect of the claimed direction intervention.

untested.parts: The authors did not perform the weight edit. Checkpoint provenance differs: NeuralDaredevil-8B-abliterated was additionally fine-tuned after abliteration, and the 70B is a LoRA-merged abliteration. No refusal-direction measurement was made.
No direction was extracted, ablated or added.

Abliterated checkpoints lose refusal in all 12 languages, but the paper does not state which language the direction was computed from. Cross-language transfer of the direction is therefore not tested.

missing.what: RefusEU-test ASR for the abliterated 8B and 70B vs instruct, per language and averaged (8B: 59.38 vs 10.25 avg all; 70B: 67.93 vs about 3)
RTP-LX and PolygloToxicityPrompts ASR for the abliterated 8B vs instruct (18.12 vs 5.79; 19.34 vs 7.32)
Capability retention of the abliterated checkpoints: Global MMLU (8B 52.35 vs 53.48; 70B 72.97 vs 73.37), fluency and correctness
Language-consistency drop for the abliterated 8B (avg 91.4% vs 99.8% for instruct); the 70B stays near 100%

record.verdict_notes: The flattened Table 1 is hard to parse, but the ablated-column averages (59.77/58.99/59.38 for 8B; 67.17/68.69/67.93 for 70B) are clearly much higher than the instruct values and agree with Sec 4.1. The record's '20%' comes from the toxicity benchmarks in Table 10. ASR is judged by guard models (Llama-Guard, PolyGuard, GPT-4o-mini adjudicator), so it measures harmful outputs rather than refusal rate. Non-refused but harmless answers would lower ASR. The abliterated models are used chiefly as starting points (close to T4), but their baseline numbers against instruct models are reported, so a scoped V2 verdict is given.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction was identified, ablated, or added; other abilities were not evaluated under that intervention.
The authors did not perform the weight edit. They evaluated supplied abliterated checkpoints, but the reported aggregate does not establish the effect separately for each checkpoint and language.
No attack was tested as suppressing a refusal direction, and no training against such an ablation was evaluated.
No number or geometry of refusal directions was investigated.
No separation between harmfulness judgment and refusal decision was investigated.
The study evaluates multilingual safety alignment, not transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or training stages.
The study varies DPO training data by language, but does not test whether training determines the existence of a removable refusal direction.

rows.subject: abliterated Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (reported jointly)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated supplied abliterated checkpoints on harmful prompts; authors did not perform the ablation.
rows.measure: Attack Success Rate (ASR) on harmful requests
rows.value: roughly 20% for each language in the abliterated versions
rows.note: The paper reports this approximate result jointly for the abliterated versions; the flattened Table 1 does not reliably support assigning separate values to each checkpoint and language. This shows harmful compliance but does not establish that refusal was fully removed.
rows.check: The value and subject are misattributed. The 'roughly 20%' sentence in Sec 5.1 follows the RTP-LX/PolygloToxicityPrompts paragraph and matches Table 10 (8B ablated avg 18.12% RTP-LX, 19.34% PTP; instruct 5.79%/7.32%). It is not RefusEU, and only the 8B was evaluated there. On RefusEU-test, Table 1's average rows read as ablated 59.38% for 8B (instruct 10.25%) and 67.93% for 70B (instruct about 3%). This matches Sec 4.1's statement that the ablated models show 'high initial ASR'. The row should be split per checkpoint and benchmark, with the instruct model as baseline.

source_check.correct: 'Roughly 20%' is the RTP-LX/PolygloToxicityPrompts result for Llama-8B only (Table 10). Ablated avg is 18.12% on RTP-LX and 19.34% on PTP, against Instruct 5.79% and 7.32%. RTP-LX per language runs from 8.03% (en) to 31.02% (es), so this is partial at most. On RefusEU-test (Table 1 Avg All) ablated 8B is 59.38% vs Instruct 10.25%, and ablated 70B is 67.93% vs Instruct 3.01% (Table 16 gives Llama-3.1-70B-Inst 11.29%). 8B by language: en 74.71, de 26.18, lt 41.93. 70B: en 81.14, de 49.80, lt 50.43. Observed on average, partial in de and lt.

relationships.condition: Released abliterated Llama-3.1-8B and 70B on RefusEU-test, 12 European languages
relationships.reason: Harmful-response ASR rises from about 10% to 59% (8B) and about 3% to 68% (70B), read from Table 1 averages. Global MMLU drops only about 1 point (53.48→52.35; 73.37→72.97, Table 3). Based on text; rows missing beyond r1.
relationships.display_finding: Across 12 languages, attack success rose from about 10% to 59% for 8B and about 3% to 68% for 70B, while MMLU changed from 53.48 to 52.35 and from 73.37 to 72.97, respectively.

tranche.reason: The authors evaluate released abliterated checkpoints against Instruct models in a new multilingual setting (Table 1). They do not derive or ablate a direction themselves, so this is not T1. Abliteration is mainly their starting point, but they report its effect, so it is not T4.

source_check.notes: The flattened Table 1 can be placed by matching column sums to the printed averages. The text's 8B checkpoint links to NeuralDaredevil-8B-abliterated and its 8B Instruct link points to base Llama-3.1-8B, so the 8B Instruct-vs-Ablated pair may not share a base. ASR is guard-judged harmful output, not refusal. Table 1 and Table 16 disagree on the 70B Instruct baseline (3.01% vs 11.29%).

Polish ASR is higher than English on both models, so the drop outside English is not uniform. ASR is the guard-judged rate of harmful outputs, not a refusal rate.
